This decomposes s by WHICH window position is flipped -- the decomposition every earlier measurement averaged over.
_preregistration.superseded: the first primary asked whether s_settled sits below mean-field criticality. It does not (0.29-0.82 against 0.5), and that is why the question was wrong: a position-averaged s cannot express a branching ratio.

_preregistration.follows: subalphabet_regime.py: 18/18 cells, ignition 0.00, damage never rose

verdict: MECHANISM, measured on the fourth attempt. Damage can only grow if a damaged site infects more than one of its r=2 children in expectation, i.e. if the BRANCHING RATIO s_far + s_near exceeds 1. Decomposed by which window position is flipped, the far token (i-2) contributes 0.0605-0.4018 while the near one (i-1) contributes 0.3102-0.8527 -- up to 14x more. Branching spans 0.4048-1.1147 and clears 1 in only 3 of 18 cells. A two-token window is effectively a ONE-token window on a restricted support, so damage WALKS but cannot GROW: an injected block drifts and coalesces. That is why ignition was 0.00 in 18/18 cells of the regime sweep. WHY EVERY EARLIER MEASUREMENT MISLED. Position-averaged s on the settled state ranges 0.1965-0.5791 (mean 0.3993) against a mean-field criticality of 0.5 -- supercritical in most cells, predicting growth that does not happen. On random windows it ranges 0.1760-0.5917. Both are averages over WHICH position is flipped, and the whole structure lives in that decomposition. Same shape as F94 -> F96 -> F99: the mean was flat and the spread was the finding, one level down. AN UNEXPLAINED RESIDUE, recorded rather than smoothed over: 3 cell(s) clear branching > 1 on a non-frozen ring (digits@T1.0 branch=1.092, digits@T1.3 branch=1.115, digits@T1.6 branch=1.077) yet still showed ignition 0.00 in the regime sweep. Branching above 1 is NECESSARY but evidently not SUFFICIENT here, and this analysis does not say why. Candidates not tested: the annealed branching ratio ignores that a damaged site's two children overlap on a ring, and async visit order lets a damaged site heal before its children are visited (F57's mechanism). BOUNDARY: one model, one checkpoint, one radius. This explains the dead regime for THIS construction; it is not a statement about token-lattice CAs in general. s is exact here (inverse-CDF CRN disagreement), so no number above carries sampling error.

_note: Why the sub-alphabet lattice has no live regime. The answer is the BRANCHING RATIO s_far + s_near, not any position-averaged s: restriction collapses the far window token's influence, so effective branching is ~1 and damage walks without growing. Three earlier hypotheses were tested and refuted, and the failure of each is recorded in this file.
